newsitem.title: CHINA: China leveraged buy-outs seen promising.
newsitem.headline: China leveraged buy-outs seen promising.

text.p: China may be able to use leveraged buy-outs as a way of strengthening ailing state enterprises, a Chinese financial specialist said on Monday.
"I see a promising future for leveraged buy-outs," said Wang Ran, managing director of Eastern Wall Street, a Chinese financial consulting company.
Wang told a seminar on asset management that companies that did not have huge debt burdens could be targets for acquisitions under leveraged buy-outs.
"These should be market-driven deals," he said. "They should not be made under government order."
A leveraged buy-out can occur when funds are raised to take over a company and the target company's assets are used as collateral for the borrowing.

Wang said several major hurdles would have to be cleared, such as the relatively underdeveloped market for corporate debt, cautiousness of domestic banks and government concerns over the possible loss of state assets.

Leveraged buy-outs could be more easily completed if both the acquiring company and the takeover target were state firms. That would reduce state concerns over the possible loss of state assets, he said.
Wang also said a possible strategy would be to have the acquired company take out bank credits backed by its own assets as collateral. The acquiring company would eventually make repayment.
China is trying to aid its ailing state sector companies by encouraging mergers or selling some of them to the private sector.
Many state companies, protected by the government under years of central planning, have been unable to compete with private firms in the sink-or-swim marketplace.
